conviction_note: The -43.67% 20-day slide is not fundamental news — it is the unwind of the CEO's own 10b5-1 accumulation programme, which stopped dead on 2026-08-13 after five months of near-weekly buying and has bought nothing through a 46% decline; that removes the 'bad news already priced in' cushion the run-up implies and leaves a small net negative, sized well inside the 8.45% historical-median anchor because the interpretation of the plan's termination is genuinely two-sided.

findings.finding: CEO/10%-owner Jack Jiajia Huang bought COE ADSs on the open market under a Rule 10b5-1 plan almost every week from April through 2026-08-13 (about 29 Form 4s between 04-13 and 08-21, longest gap ~8 days, purchases at $25.74 on 05-29, $16.45-16.72 on 07-06/07/08, $19.61-$20.83 on 08-11/12/13), and has filed nothing since 2026-08-21 — 17 trading sessions and a 46% decline to $10.60 with zero purchases — while last quarter the same plan was buying on 06-05 and filing on 06-10, two days before the 06-12 Q1 release, proving the plan is not suspended by an earnings blackout.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-14 (EDGAR filing index; most recent Form 4 filed 2026-08-21, accession 0002029760-26-000009, period of report 2026-04-10, acceptance 2026-08-21 06:48:20; prior filing 0002029760-26-000008 reports 08-11 and 08-12 purchases; 0001104659-26-072099 filed 2026-06-10 reports purchases 05-29 through 06-05)
findings.why_not_priced: The market demonstrably reacted to the buying and cannot react to its absence: StockTitan headlines every Form 4 ('Insider buying at 51Talk (COE): CEO-linked entities add 1,444,920 shares') and COE rallied 33% from $16.00 on 07-31 to a $21.32 high on 08-13 across exactly the sessions the plan was lifting 18-20% of daily volume, then round-tripped to below where it started once the filings stopped. Nobody publishes a non-filing, so the withdrawal of that bid produced a monotonic 48% slide on 7k-90k ADS/day with no crash day. If the market had priced this, the slide would have come on a datable gap day with a news catalyst and there would be commentary attributing it; instead EDGAR full-text search returns no 6-K, no F-3, no 13D/A and no company filing of any kind between the 06-12 Q1 6-K and today, and no analyst action is findable. The second-order consequence is the part that matters tomorrow: the baseline hands the market a -43.67% run-up that reads as 'priced for disaster, primed to bounce', and the free control -run_up_20d_pct would rank COE among the day's strongest longs on that number alone — but the decline carries no fundamental information, so there is no disappointment discount to relieve, and no price-insensitive buyer left to absorb a soft print in a ~4m ADS float.
findings.independence: The price and volume series that makes the mechanism visible is a separate source from EDGAR: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/coe/history/ (fetched 2026-09-14) shows $16.00 close 07-31, $20.60 on 08-13, then an uninterrupted slide to $10.60 on 09-10 on 7,182-89,848 ADS/day with no single gap. NOTE: the 'insider stopped buying' reading and the 'run-up is mechanical, not informational' reading rest on the same Form 4 cluster plus that price series, so they are deliberately filed as ONE finding rather than two.

findings.finding: Q1 2026 cash fell $3.5m (from $39.0m to $35.5m) even though advances from students rose $2.4m (from $76.569m to $78.930m) and the operating loss was only $1.4m — roughly $4.4m of cash outflow that the published results cannot account for — and 51Talk publishes no cash flow statement with its earnings releases, against a shareholders' deficit of -$33.579m (total assets $65.327m, total liabilities $98.809m) and a $66m market cap.
findings.why_not_priced: One estimate exists on this $66m name and no sell-side preview does; the wire-level coverage of the Q1 print was 'revenue +70.9%, active students +63.9%' (StockTitan, TipRanks) and the headline on the coming print will be billings against the $36-38m guide and EPS. If the balance-sheet composition were priced you would see previews framed around the cash line and the $78.9m student-prepayment liability rather than around growth rates, and the $10m buyback authorised in December 2025 would not have been the last balance-sheet item any aggregator mentioned. Cash is 54% of market cap and the reconciliation gap is unresolvable from anything the company publishes, so the Q2 cash balance — a number no consensus covers — is the swing item in tomorrow's release, and a repeat of the Q1 gap takes cash to ~$31m against an unchanged delivery obligation.
findings.independence: Independent confirmation of the negative equity from a different source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-services/nysemkt-coe/51talk-online-education-group (accessed 2026-09-14) reports negative equity of -US$33m. Separately, I checked and REJECTED the obvious inference: NYSE American Company Guide Sec. 1003(a)(i)-(iii) does not bite here because FY2025 total assets ($66.1m) and revenue ($95.6m) both exceed $50m, satisfying the alternative test, so there is no listing-deficiency finding to make.

findings.finding: 51Talk launched Saudi-specific courseware built on licensed Oxford University Press content at the Saudi 2026 Back-to-School Exhibition on 14-17 August 2026, fronted by national brand ambassador Yasser Al-Hazimi, off a Middle East hub opened in Riyadh in 2025 — a higher-ARPU demand geography that is nowhere in the company's own Q1 call, which contained no geographic commentary at all.
findings.why_not_priced: It ran in Saudi Gazette and regional aggregators, not on the US tape, and the company's own Q1 earnings call transcript contains zero references to Saudi Arabia, the Middle East, the Philippines, Indonesia or Malaysia — management has given US holders no geographic decomposition to attach it to. If this were priced, the sell-side framing would be about a Gulf ARPU mix shift rather than about a Philippines teacher-supply story, and the 70.9% revenue growth against 63.9% student growth in Q1 (i.e. ARPU doing real work) would be the number being previewed. Small size because it is a Q3 event that can only reach tomorrow's print through forward commentary, and no enrolment or revenue figure is attached to it anywhere.

baseline_tension: It cuts hard against the run-up: the baseline's -43.67% 20-day decline and 4.5%-off-the-52-week-low positioning invite a mean-reversion long (and the free control -run_up_20d_pct would rank COE among the day's biggest longs), but the Form 4 record shows that decline is the unwind of the CEO's own August buying rather than fundamental repricing, so there is no priced-in disappointment to relieve and the marginal bid is gone — and with no option chain the baseline's 8.45% 'expected move' is a stale-regime median against 71.8% realised vol and recent -13.5%/-6.9%/-6.6% daily prints, so the true distribution is far wider than my central number.
